title: Agent and Skill Design
summary: Define FlowDoc agent roles, capabilities, handoffs, real PLAN and WORK room delivery flow, N WORK rooms orchestration, Work Type routing, Context Capsules, Context Acknowledgement, mandatory WORK room return, automatic WORK-to-PLAN return, active WORK-to-PLAN return push, PLAN-owned reporting, Revision Packets, Lean Dispatch resource-budget rules, final Lean Dispatch multi-WORK smoke behavior, the Project Control grouped test gate, the source-docs subgroup gate, and reusable skills after the documentation authority cleanup evidence by turning root-cause analysis into operating rules, role overlays, handoff requirements, delivery round boundaries, PLAN room dispatch/review rules, completionQueue ordering, same-room revision handling, manual recovery boundaries, lean token/review cost controls, Project Control records/source-docs/app gate stability, focused source-docs gate routing, and reusable skill boundaries.
expectedOutput: Project Control records FlowDoc agent documentation authority operating rules, the Delivery Operating Model for real PLAN/WORK room coordination, PLAN Room Orchestration Rules for dispatching and reviewing N WORK rooms, the Work Type Routing Model for lane classification, Context Capsule handoff, Context Acknowledgement, mandatory WORK room return, automatic WORK-to-PLAN return, active WORK-to-PLAN return push, PLAN task/chat ID, Active Return Command, liveness tracking, silent room handling, retrievable locator, PLAN-owned reporting, acceptanceGate revision decisions, Revision Packet loop, completionQueue, returnOrderPolicy, arrivalSequence, duplicate handoff handling, manual recovery fallback boundaries, Lean Dispatch resource controls including contextBudget, verificationTier, reviewTier, evidenceMode, handoffDetail, docReadPolicy, Reference Packs, compact Terminal Handoffs, escalation triggers, Project Control check:grouped and test:unit grouped gate scripts, focused source-docs subgroup scripts including test:source-docs:core-migration, test:source-docs:live-draft, test:source-docs:template-builder, test:source-docs:text-block, and test:source-docs:text-engine, and skill candidate routing, and the first local flowdoc-project-control Codex skill package so future FlowDoc rooms route through Project Control before generic planning paths, while keeping broader specialized skill packaging for later phases.
riskSummary: The first local entrypoint skill, global guidance, Delivery Operating Model, PLAN Room Orchestration Rules, Work Type Routing Model, Lean Dispatch Operating Rules, Project Control grouped test gate, and source-docs subgroup gate reduce Markdown authority, handoff, context, token, liveness, acceptance, revision, automatic return, active return push, queue ordering, evidence batching, verification-cost, default parallel full Project Control unit gate timeout, source-docs whole-group overuse, and room coordination drift risk. The single-room active return smoke test proves one projectless WORK room on this local host can push a Terminal Handoff back to PLAN with mcp__codex_app.send_message_to_thread, the multi-WORK active return queue smoke test proves two read-only projectless WORK rooms can push distinct handoffs to the same PLAN task and be processed through completionQueue with arrivalSequence 1 and 2, the product-repository read-only active return smoke test proves a worktree-created Core task can resolve from clientThreadId to a real task and push a no-op handoff back to PLAN, and the final Lean Dispatch multi-WORK same-room Revision Packet smoke proves two projectless no-edit lean WORK rooms can return to PLAN automatically while PLAN classifies one first return as needs-revision, sends a Revision Packet back to the same WORK room, and receives a revised PASS handoff, while actual product edits remain unproven by read-only or projectless smokes. The Backend product-edit active return smoke proves one product WORK room with actual Backend edits can push its Terminal Handoff back to PLAN and be accepted through PLAN-owned reporting. Project Control check:grouped now keeps data validation, type-check, serial grouped unit tests, build, and e2e in the default gate while preserving test:unit:parallel as a non-default exploratory fast path. source-docs core-migration remains the heaviest subgroup and may need deeper profiling if Core documentation lanes keep dominating PLAN verification time. clientThreadId-only dispatch remains unsafe before PLAN resolves a monitorable task/chat locator. Local skills may not be installed or surfaced in every future environment, bounded pressure validation does not prove future agent compliance, multi-product-WORK close-together return remains unproven, future automatic room wakeups remain unproven, product WORK rooms may still self-promote if a future packet omits PLAN-owned reporting, a PLAN room may still send an incomplete Context Capsule or over-lean packet, manual recovery may still require user-provided recovery context, a silent room may still need recovery classification, and the agent-and-skill-design work itself does not promote Core, Backend, or Editor product truth.
